title: Banking Sales System
summary: A bank's product-sales and transaction platform: customer onboarding with KYC, an order/application workflow, a double-entry ledger as the source of truth, idempotent payments, and an auditable event trail with end-of-day reconciliation.

blocks.text: Framing: design the system a bank uses to sell products (accounts, cards, loans, FDs) to customers through branches, relationship managers and digital channels, and to process the resulting money movements.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Product catalogue and eligibility; applications and approvals (credit checks)
Fund transfers, payments, fees, interest postings
Sales pipeline for RMs (leads, opportunities, commissions); statements
Money is never created, lost or double-posted (strong consistency)
Full audit trail; regulatory reporting; data residency
99.95%+ availability for payments; idempotent APIs end to end

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Throughput is modest by internet standards; the design is driven by correctness, auditability and peak days like salary credits and month-end interest runs.

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Store money as integers in minor units or DECIMAL — never floating point. Postings are immutable; corrections are new reversing entries.

blocks.caption: Channels → domain services → ledger as the single source of truth

items: Customer onboarding stores documents, runs KYC/AML checks asynchronously, and sets kycStatus.
Application workflow (orchestrated saga): eligibility → credit check → underwriting decision → account creation in the core ledger → card issuance / disbursement.
Transfers: gateway checks the idempotency key; payments service posts to the ledger in one ACID transaction; external rails are called via outbox with retries and reconciliation.
Events feed CRM (commissions, sales dashboards), notifications, fraud and the regulatory warehouse.

items.title: Credit check
items.text: Call bureau; cache report; timeout + retry.

items.title: Decision
items.text: Rules engine + model; manual review queue for edge cases.

items.title: Disbursed
items.text: Post disbursement entry; outbox → rails; compensate on failure.

items: State machine persisted per application with version numbers; every transition audited with actor and reason.
Human tasks (maker-checker approvals) are steps with SLAs and escalation.
Compensation: if disbursement fails at the rail, reverse the posting with a new journal entry and notify.

sections.title: Deep dive: external payments and reconciliation

items: Two-step posting: debit customer to a **suspense/clearing account** first, then settle when the rail confirms; failure reverses from suspense.
Rails are at-least-once and sometimes ambiguous (timeouts): query status by our reference before retrying.
End-of-day reconciliation: match our ledger postings with rail settlement files and bank statements; breaks go to an operations queue.
Batch jobs (interest accrual, fees) run as idempotent chunks keyed by (account, date), restartable.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The ledger is the source of truth; everything else is a projection. Any external call that moves money is idempotent, goes through a suspense account, and is reconciled daily.

sections.title: Deep dive: security, compliance and audit

items: PII encrypted at rest with KMS; field-level encryption for IDs (PAN, Aadhaar); tokenization for card numbers (PCI DSS).
RBAC + maker-checker for high-risk actions; least privilege; break-glass access logged.
Audit log append-only with hash chaining (each record hashes the previous) for tamper evidence; retained per regulation (years).
Data residency (e.g. RBI data localization for payment data); DR site in-country; RPO ≈ 0 for ledger via synchronous replication.
Fraud: real-time scoring on transfers (velocity, device, geo), step-up auth (OTP) for risky ones.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Sub-accounts / sharded balances; batch posting to GL
Queue bulk credits, process in parallel by account shard
Sync replication to DR, tested failover drills

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Security, DR, fraud, metrics: unreconciled breaks, saga age.

items.q: How do you shard a ledger?
items.a: By account_id; a transfer between shards becomes a saga with a suspense/clearing account on each shard, or both accounts are routed to a shard pair; most banks keep core ledgers on a strongly consistent cluster.

items.q: How do you compute a balance quickly?
items.a: Maintain a balances table updated in the same transaction; periodically verify it equals the sum of postings.
Postings per currency; an FX entry debits INR and credits USD through FX position accounts at a recorded rate.

items.q: How would you design RM commissions?
items.a: Consume ApplicationApproved/AccountFunded events into a commissions service with rules per product; idempotent by application ID.

items: Double-entry: every entry's postings sum to zero.
Money in integer minor units or DECIMAL.
Idempotency keys on every money-moving API.
Suspense accounts for external rails; daily reconciliation.
Orchestrated sagas for applications; maker-checker steps.
Immutable postings; corrections are reversals.
Hash-chained audit log; encryption + tokenization.
